newsitem.title: GERMANY: U-Freight will invest more in terminals, technolog.
newsitem.headline: U-Freight will invest more in terminals, technolog.

text.p: International freight forwarder U-Freight said it will push ahead with large-scale investment in terminals, technology and new services this year.
New facilities will be opened in China, other Asian destinations and Europe, senior managers said at the recent U-Freight European sales meeting in Munich attended by 21 company managers.
N.S. Cheong, U-Freight owner and director, said the forwarder generated sales revenue of $250 million in 1996, excluding separate operations of franchisees and agents.
More than $30 million had been invested in recent years and this would be continued in the future, he added.
U-Freight now has 57 offices in 17 countries, with Asia and trans-Pacific as its strongest markets.

U-Freight opened a $22 million Singapore freight centre and new facilities in the Philippines, Japan and Australia last year and had spent four million dollars on computer systems in recent years, Cheong said.
Gene Boyer, U-Freight managing director Americas & Europe, said the company was considering opening a centre at the former Clark Bay base on the Philippines within the next 18 months.
In the U.S., U-Freight has opened a New Jersey office to target the international publishing industry, he added.
The forwarder is also a member of the Global Book Network, a specialist book shipping and logistics association, and offered door-to-door pricing for the industry.
In Europe, U-Freight had a Dutch subsidiary, franchisees in Britain, Ireland, Germany and Italy and agents for the rest of Europe.
New facilities are planned at two British sites later this year. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
